look_here_first: HAIRY WOOLLYGRASS: low perennial dryland bunchgrass with compact woolly-looking flowering clusters composed of several small overlapping spikelets. Look at the obvious silky white hairs on bracts with 10× magnification, then check glume and lemma details to separate other short tuft grasses. The original project owner's private-rights image is NOT used in the public genus lesson.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole rooted low grass clump in dry soil
One fluffy spikelet face and edge, glume vs lemma bract at 10–20x
True ligule and blade base with millimeter rule
Side-by-side Tridens or Muhlenbergia compared spikelet
crew_field_check: Unlike Tridens texanus or other more open-flowered tridens-type grasses, Erioneuron makes short crowded woolly heads; distinguish hairy glumes and fertile lemmas under magnification. Do not identify from an unfocused distant grassy clump.
Confirm true collar, ripe spikelets and habit from the same source-identified individual.
